decisions.reason: Extro’s possession of an immortal does not establish a durable material-support regime.
decisions.analysis: The discovery phrase immortals under Extro conflates a conflict with an established civilian economy; the Group’s individual pursuits do not prove automated provision.

decisions.reason: Automated-system dependence is verified as a theme, but actual production and allocation remain unclear.
decisions.analysis: Alienation, segregation and computing do not by themselves establish labor-independent necessities or deliberate retention of dispensable work.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper reading; an inaccessible SF Reviews page was not recovered through another route.

decisions.reason: Shalmaneser assists corporate power without a verified post-work distribution mechanism.
decisions.analysis: Planning and information processing are not equivalent to automatic production and common access.
decisions.follow_up: Keep as an AI-assisted corporate-economy comparison.

decisions.reason: Information networks, government handouts and Precipice’s shared human work do not establish an automated support economy.
decisions.analysis: Paid-avoidance compensation follows infrastructure withdrawal; the identifiable alternative enclave still practices agrarian and cottage-industry work.
decisions.follow_up: Keep as an information-power and community comparison.

decisions.reason: The short ending account presents redistributive proposals and a vote rather than a verified durable post-worm economy.
decisions.analysis: Open information and proposed wage/distribution rules do not establish an already functioning labor-independent arrangement.
decisions.follow_up: Skip ending reconstruction; do not score a referendum’s proposed outcome as enacted.

decisions.reason: Environmental consumer collapse does not itself meet the automated-production admission rule.
decisions.analysis: Scarcity, pollution and corporate malfeasance cannot substitute for a demonstrated post-work or job-preservation mechanism.

decisions.reason: Automated paid services and a depleted personal fortune do not establish a continuing supported population.
decisions.analysis: Forrester needs employment after spending his insurance capital. A finite windfall plus robot purchases is not an implemented automation-funded lifetime cohort arrangement.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper reading rather than generalizing from one revived consumer.

decisions.reason: The identified Venus society is a precarious working tourist economy without verified post-work access.
decisions.analysis: The tour operator’s medical need and search for profit do not reveal a general automatic provision or unnecessary-employment system.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper reading; later Heechee technologies are separate.

decisions.reason: The later pleasure civilization is identified, but its material-production and access system remains unverified.
decisions.analysis: A comfortable high-technology habitat and remote time jump cannot settle the distribution rules or ownership of production.
decisions.follow_up: Skip reconstruction across the novel’s many epochs.

decisions.reason: Watch Wheel manufacture does not establish a general post-work Heechee society.
decisions.analysis: CHON food and handling robots are real, but the station has duty rotations and a mixed population. Broad Heechee access and a justified alien-person proxy remain unclear.
decisions.follow_up: Skip a whole-novel investigation; preserve the bounded manufacture evidence without inventing general rights.

review_notes: Ten quick dispositions; bounded indexed excerpts only where returned directly by the short searches.
No broad entitlement is inferred from a finite inheritance, a duty station, longevity or a proposed closing referendum.
The inaccessible Jagged Orbit review was not bypassed; other accessible critical context remains honestly limited.
All unretained cases have explicit reasons and follow-up limits, rather than silent queue omissions.
